newsitem.title: HAITI: U.S. police to join U.N. mission in Haiti.
newsitem.headline: U.S. police to join U.N. mission in Haiti.

text.p: About 25 U.S. policemen will join the United Nations police mission in Haiti, bringing the force to near full strength at a time of increased political tension, a U.N. spokesman said Wednesday.

A total of 270 police officers from seven countries are now in Haiti training a new police force. The new contingent will bring the U.N. numbers to just under 300, the size approved by the Security Council.
"We have always been looking to further contributions because we need all 300 monitors," U.N. spokesman Eric Falt said.
Former military leader Joseph-Jean Baptiste was arrested over the weekend in connection with an arms cache found hidden in the house of former paramilitary leader Emmanual "Toto" Constant.
Also found were detailed plans for destabilising the government, including targeting officials for assassination, according to Haitian police chief Pierre Denize.
